subject: Request: post-audit coverage assertion and evidence plan
messages:
From: Natalie Price <natalie.price@evergenthealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@evergenthealth.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 post-report coverage assertion (request)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team is finalizing the vendor packet and has one outstanding ask before contract signature: a written assertion (bridge/continuity note) that covers the period between Redwood's last SOC 2 Type II report (period end 2025-12-31) and today. We need confirmation that there were no changes to the control environment that would materially affect the report, plus a short list of evidence we can reference for our security team (key controls, KMS usage, incident history).

Can you provide a bridge letter or an interim coverage note and a plan for delivering supporting artifacts? Procurement would like this by COB Tuesday 2026-07-13 to keep our signature timeline.

Appreciate it —
Natalie
Natalie Price
Vendor Risk Manager, Evergent Health Systems
procurement@evergenthealth.com
From: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: Natalie Price <natalie.price@evergenthealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 post-report coverage assertion (request)

Natalie —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can provide a short interim coverage letter that: (1) states the SOC 2 report period and the post-report date range we are asserting coverage for, (2) confirms no unremediated control changes were introduced that would affect the report's conclusions, and (3) lists the items we can share as evidence (SOC 2 report PDF, KMS usage snapshot, change-control summary, and a short incident log for the period).

Before I send a draft, two quick clarifications to make sure the note meets your procurement/security checklist:
- Do you need the bridge letter to be signed by our VP of Security (we typically have it signed by Security + Legal for procurement asks)?
- Is a redacted KMS access log (user, date, action) sufficient, or does your team need raw logs in a secure transfer?

We have a draft bridge letter and the SOC 2 Type II PDF ready; I can attach the draft and an evidence checklist now and push final signed letter by Monday close of day. If procurement requires DocuSign before Tuesday, I will escalate to Legal.

Drafts attached: redwood_soc2_type2_20251231.pdf (redacted), draft_bridge_letter_sept2025.docx (draft).

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
From: Natalie Price <natalie.price@evergenthealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@evergenthealth.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 post-report coverage assertion (request)

Sean —

Thanks — signature by VP of Security is preferred but not strictly required; if Legal signs that's acceptable. For logs: a redacted KMS access snapshot (username/email, timestamp, action) delivered as CSV is fine for initial review. Procurement will request any additional raw telemetry later, but needs the letter + CSV to close the file.

One more ask: can the bridge letter explicitly state the asserted post-report period (2026-01-01 through 2026-07-12) and that there were no material changes to access control, encryption key management, or incident history in that window? Also include contact information for the person who can walk through the evidence (that can be you or someone on the security team).

If you can provide a DocuSign link for signature, procurement will route it immediately.

Best,
Natalie
From: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com

Natalie —

Attachment: kms_access_logs_202601-202606.csv (redacted stub).

Attached is the redacted KMS access snapshot you requested and a second draft of the interim coverage letter. Key points in the letter:
- Report: SOC 2 Type II (period ended 2025-12-31)
- Asserted coverage window: 2026-01-01 through 2026-07-12
- Statement: No unremediated or material changes to access control, encryption key management, or production incident handling during the asserted window that would alter the conclusions of the SOC 2 report.
- Evidence we can provide on request: SOC 2 report PDF, KMS access snapshot (attached), change-control summary (internal change log extract), and incident summary (high-level).

Per your preference we will route the letter for signature by VP of Security and Legal. I have sent the draft to Legal and cc'd Priyom for procurement coordination. If that works, I'll initiate the DocuSign envelope and share the link by EOD.

Action items:
- Priyom: confirm procurement details and whether procurement needs the envelope sent to a distribution list.
- Natalie: confirm the asserted window (above) is acceptable; if yes we'll send DocuSign.

Thanks —
Sean
